facts.statement: Fossils of Incolornis were discovered in the Bissekty Formation in Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: Remains have been found in the Bissekty Formation in Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: The genus is known only from fragmentary coracoid bones.
facts.quote: It is only known from fragmentary coracoids.

facts.statement: Incolornis lived during the Coniacian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 89 and 86 million years ago.
facts.quote: Incolornis (meaning "inhabitant bird") is an extinct genus of basal birds from the Late Cretaceous (Coniacian, 89–86 mya).

facts.statement: I. silvae was estimated to be 135 mm long, while I. martini was estimated to be 220 mm long.
facts.quote: The estimated length of these animals was 135 mm for I. silvae and 220 mm for I. martini.

facts.statement: The systematic position of Incolornis is unclear, though it may belong to the Enantiornithes.
facts.quote: The systematic position of the genus is unclear; it might have been an enantiornithine bird.

facts.statement: Incolornis is classified within the parent group Alexornithidae.
Incolornis belongs to the family Alexornithidae.
The time range for Incolornis is estimated from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)
